family.title: Multi-rune feedback and autokey
family.question: Do fixed multi-rune feedback rules produce English-like page outputs?

title: Two-to-six-rune feedback and autokey screen
question: Do seven fixed multi-rune history functions under ciphertext, plaintext or mixed feedback yield an English-like LP2 reading in the published finite grid?
reader_question: Could each rune be decoded using a key derived from the preceding runes?
summary: The 23,520-setting source sweep found no convincing English reading. A separate power check shows its actual all-equal-seed search misses its own plaintext- and mixed-history plants.
finding: The source grid best is -6.299 on a 66-rune segment, below the -5.500 advancement bar. Its 21 controls recover when supplied their exact non-equal seed. Under the real search's all-equal seeds, 7/7 ciphertext-history plants recover, but 0/7 plaintext-history and 0/7 mixed-history plants do. The negative is limited to the executed grid and is not a power-validated exclusion of the latter modes.
limitations: The supplemental plant check is retrospective and fixes k=3, sign -1 and the source control passage. Plaintext and mixed history used only 29 all-equal initial states out of 29^k possibilities; wrong seeds need not converge, as this measured gate confirms. The 200 raw-stream shuffles are not a best-of-23,520 null and the best candidate is a short segment. Other feedback functions, initial states, alphabets, languages and boundaries remain open.
next_steps: A concrete feedback proposal should specify its recurrence, seed, boundary reset and output language before scoring; test matched planted examples and apply the same full selection to null controls.

scope.representation: Zero-based GP rune indices from the pinned source transcription: 12,956 unsolved runes in 55 nonempty source segments, plus their concatenation.
scope.procedure: For each stream, sweep seven fixed feedback functions, k=2..6, three history sources, both signs and both directions; score decoded transliteration using the pinned English quadgram table and 29 all-equal seeds for plaintext/mixed history.
scope.parameters: 56 streams x 7 functions x 5 history lengths x 3 sources x 2 signs x 2 directions = 23,520 scored configurations. Ciphertext history ignores the seed after k; plaintext/mixed source probe eq0 through eq28. Twenty-one k=3 planted controls.
scope.exclusions: Non-equal initial seeds, k outside 2..6, formulas outside the seven-source basis, state crossing other page boundaries, skip-aware decoding, different transliterations or language scorers.

review.reviewer: Source executable replay with independent winning-rule and score calculation; independent search-domain plant audit

reproduction.environment: Python 3 standard library; pinned code and inputs are bundled. Full rerun takes several minutes.

visuals.caption: The planted English control clears the score requirement. The strongest LP2 candidate is lower.
Each rule maps two to six earlier symbols into a key value used to decode the next rune.
The source search recovers ciphertext-history controls but none of its non-equal-seed plaintext or mixed-history controls under the 29 tried all-equal seeds.

reader_finding: None of 23,520 settings reached the English-score threshold. But the search also missed all 14 planted plaintext-history and mixed-history examples when limited to its actual starting values, so that negative result cannot rule out those methods.
reader_limit: The search uses seven fixed rules, two to six earlier runes, and only starting sequences whose values are all equal. Other starting sequences and feedback rules were not searched.
